data.gender_notes: Chinu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'chinna' meaning 'grace, beauty, or young'. In Hindu mythology, Chinu is a playful name for the god Ganesha, who is known for his grace and beauty. The name Chinu carries the meaning “Grace, beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chinu usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is popular among various communities in different parts of India, particularly in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra. This name represents the joy and happiness of childhood and can be used as a term of endearment.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Chinu holds a unique spiritual significance as it is often used as a playful name for the elephant-headed god Ganesha. Chinu represents the divine child who is known for his mischief, innocence, and beauty. He is a god of wisdom, knowledge, and is the remover of obstacles. The name Chinu reflects the grace and beauty that exists within all of us, reminding us of the divine child within each one of us, encouraging us to embrace the innocence and joy of life.
